comments.body:
I'll agree that it looks weird, but this is intentional. Do I understand correctly that this only affects how the manual looks, but does not cause any other issues? Otherwise we can revert immediately.
The `<imports ...>` syntax is meant to convey that the option is available only when imported.

We could change the `< >` to `[ ]`, borrowing from XQuery conditions, but I don't think that changes the overall picture that much.

A more proper solution would be to have parallel docs infrastructure for these kinds of modules, or a more general framework for this kind of thing, but in https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/pull/430876 I've opted for a simpler implementation for the purpose of agility as we develop the Modular Service feature before deciding whether to keep it.
Apologies for the disruption here.

> Do I understand correctly that this only affects how the manual looks, but does not cause any other issues?

It breaks assumption how the options are structured. Before there where only options like `abc.def.enable`. Now we have potentially duplicated options that do not really fit the scheme of the existing options.

> The `<imports ...>` syntax is meant to convey that the option is available only when imported.

We should borrow the syntax from https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/unstable/#modular-services as anything else is a little confusing as if the namespace is being shared which it isn't.

So 

```
system.services.<name>.imports = [ pkgs.ghostunnel.services.default ];
```

or 

```
system.services.<name>.ghostunnel.package = <package>;
```

would fit better in my opinion.

Also I am wondering why the default behind services is required. We could just default to that

> system.services.<name>.ghostunnel.package = <package>;

I quite like this, certainly in the context of the searchable options. It's crucial that it clearly displays the import that's required, but then it works well.

It does make the rule to have a prefix something like `ghostunnel` a hard requirement rather than a convention.
Otherwise we can't tell from the "path" what it is, and we'd get ambiguities.
That's significant, but I think it's ok.

Should we then duplicate these for users services though?

Maybe the real answer is: this is a different module class that's not NixOS, and we create a separate page and search.nixos.org tab for it.

Creating a new page in the manual seems easy enough; have done that before.

> this is a different module class that's not NixOS, and we create a separate page and search.nixos.org tab for it.

I don't want to decide that alone but it might be the best solution here so that it is clear that those options are handled slightly different 🤔

> this is a different module class that's not NixOS, and we create a separate page and search.nixos.org tab for it.

I feel like it should be a separate section in the nixpkgs manual like Modules, Options or Services (probably Services is the best) then the nixos, nix-darwin, etc manual links back to the nixpkgs manual, [However with search I feel like it's fine to stay where it is.](https://github.com/NixOS/nixos-search/pull/1192) Because it feels like it's in the correct place to define the documentation, because it's not exactly nixos.

### Nixpkgs version

- Unstable (25.11)

### Describe the bug

```
$ man configuration.nix
OPTIONS
       You can use the following options in configuration.nix.

       <imports = [ pkgs.ghostunnel.services.default ]>
           This is a modular service[1], which can be imported into a NixOS configuration using the ‘system.services’[2] option.

           Type: submodule

           Declared by:
               <nixpkgs/nixos/modules/misc/documentation/modular-services.nix:21>

            1. https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/unstable/#modular-services
            2. https://search.nixos.org/options?channel=unstable&show=system.services&query=modular+service

       <imports = [ pkgs.ghostunnel.services.default ]>.ghostunnel.package
           Package to use for ghostunnel

           Type: package

           Declared by:
               <nixpkgs/pkgs/by-name/gh/ghostunnel/service.nix>
```

man configuration.nix
